full_judgment: There is no manner of doubt that the Special Powers Act, 1974 under which the trial of the case took place is a special law enacted for special cases in special circumstances in contradistinction to the rules of law applicable generally to all cases with which the general Code of Criminal Procedure deals. It is a complete Code in itself. Section 30(1) of the Act provides that an appeal from any order, judgment and sentence of Special Tribunal may be preferred to the High Court Division within 30 days from the date of delivery or passing thereof, but this appeal appears to have been filed under section 417(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Section 1(2) of the Code clearly lays down that the provision of the Code shall not affect any special form of procedure prescribed by any special or local law. So, when section 30(1) of the Special Powers Act has, in express terms, specifically provided for an appeal from the judgment of a Special Tribunal and a special period of limitation for filing such an appeal has been prescribed therefor, an appeal against a judgment of special Tribunal is to be filed under the provision of the said section and the general provision of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall have no application in that respect."
